History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
Tele-consult for 32-year-old engineer with 2–3-day history of wheeze and exertional shortness of breath, consistent with an acute asthma flare; salbutamol inhaler usage increased, spacer and peak-flow meter prescribed, antihistamine advised, and follow-up arranged in one week or sooner if deterioration.

History:
• Presenting complaints – Wheezing and feeling “short of breath,” onset 2–3 days ago.  
• Course – Persistent over the last few days; currently feels well at rest but breathless on walking; sometimes unable to finish sentences.  
• Associated symptoms – Dry cough (no sputum, no hemoptysis), subjective fever (single recorded temp 37 °C), no chest pain, no nocturnal symptoms, no resting dyspnea, able to climb stairs.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors – Worse with walking/exertion; no stated relieving factors other than inhaler use.  
• Review of systems – Denies chest pain, hemoptysis, nighttime awakenings; no other systemic complaints elicited.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – Childhood onset, “quite bad,” used inhalers, occasional hospital visits; no ICU admissions. Stopped regular meds ~3–4 years ago but intermittently uses salbutamol inhaler (conflict noted, see quality section).  
• Atopy – Hay fever; eczema.  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• Salbutamol inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (patient reports use “every few weeks” and pre-exercise).  
• No other regular medications.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Residence – Lives with partner.  
• Occupation – Engineer; currently working from home/sick leave due to breathlessness.  
• Smoking – Never smoker.  
• Alcohol – ~1 glass of wine every 2–3 days.  
• No recreational drug use mentioned.

Family History:
• Not discussed / not provided.

Physical Examination:
• Tele-consult; no direct exam.  
• Reported temperature: 37 °C.  
• No other vitals or objective findings available.

Investigations:
• None performed during consult.  
• Plan to obtain peak-flow readings morning and evening over the next week.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected acute asthma exacerbation
  • Likely trigger: viral infection or pollen exposure (per history of atopy).  
  • Plan:  
    – Increase salbutamol to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours PRN via spacer.  
    – Prescribe spacer; pharmacist to instruct on proper use.  
    – Prescribe peak-flow meter; patient to record readings twice daily for one week.  
    – Safety-net: If temperature rises or wheeze/shortness of breath worsens, contact clinic urgently.

Issue 2: Ongoing asthma management
  • Need for formal review of control and possible initiation of maintenance therapy (e.g., inhaled corticosteroid).  
  • Plan: Telephone/face-to-face asthma review in one week with recorded peak-flow diary.

Issue 3: Allergic rhinitis / hay fever
  • Plan: Start regular over-the-counter antihistamine (specific agent to be advised in notes).

General plan items
  • Education on inhaler technique (via pharmacist).  
  • Encourage avoidance of known triggers and monitor symptom pattern.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing/expected elements: No objective lung exam, oxygen saturation, heart rate, blood pressure; comprehensive medication reconciliation limited; no family history recorded.  
• Internal conflicts: Patient states asthma meds stopped 3–4 years ago but also reports “normal” salbutamol use every few weeks and before exercise – conflict noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor repetitions/inaudible pauses but clinically adequate.
